scientific_object.title: Cross-type constraint integration burden in text-guided 3D scene generation
scientific_object.question: Holding total constraint count and instruction length fixed, does mixing heterogeneous constraint types create an integration penalty in text-guided 3D scene generation beyond the additive difficulty of the individual constraint types?
scientific_object.irreducible_object: A non-additive cross-type integration effect over the four released LEGO-Bench constraint classes. The candidate is not the statement that longer prompts or more constraints are harder; it asks whether simultaneously satisfying heterogeneous Floor Layout, Material Selection, Object Selection, and Object Placement requirements creates a residual failure burden after the same-information additive type-difficulty null is given the identical released metadata.
scientific_object.exact_ex_ante_prediction: Within each generator, after controlling instruction word count, total constraint count, analyst-defined metadata block, and flexible additive main effects for the four per-type constraint counts, higher released constraint-type entropy will predict lower official per-constraint Partial Success Rate. The effect must also have the same negative direction in the pre-outcome strict matched-pair panel. If the additive same-information null absorbs the entropy effect, the candidate is falsified.
scientific_object.strongest_same_information_baseline: An additive generalized model using the same instruction word count, total constraint count, metadata block, generator identity, and four per-type constraint counts with flexible univariate effects, but no cross-type interaction term.
scientific_object.prediction_disagreement: The additive null predicts that performance is explained by the sum of type-specific difficulty and ordinary load/length effects; the candidate predicts an additional negative cross-type integration residual when multiple constraint classes must be satisfied jointly.
scientific_object.scope_boundary: This is an independently proposed cross-substrate object. It is not a reproduction of VWE-Bench, not evidence about VWE author outcomes, and not yet a causal mechanism claim.

substrate.benchmark_unit: one released natural-language scene instruction with manually decomposed constraints
substrate.secondary_endpoint_reason: Holistic success is a conjunction over all constraints and is therefore expected to have stronger floor/load effects; it cannot be the sole primary endpoint for the integration hypothesis.

condition_type_entropy.definition: Shannon entropy in bits over the four official released constraint types

strict_matched_f0.role: future bounded robustness/falsifier panel only if independently authorized

construct_preflight.metadata_parser_note: Released labels are bound to constraints by condition_idx, matching the official evaluator. Rows 121, 127, and 129 demonstrate that label list order itself is not a valid binding rule.

candidate_generator_suite.note: Exact executable revisions, assets, provider/runtime dependencies, and output format compatibility must be frozen by a later substrate preflight. Naming a published comparison method does not authorize its execution.

future_analysis_contract_if_authorized.primary_population: all 130 released LEGO-Bench instructions for each independently qualified generator
future_analysis_contract_if_authorized.primary_model: per-constraint success modeled with generator identity, instruction word count, total constraint count, analyst-defined metadata block, and flexible additive main effects for each of the four per-type counts; test a pre-registered cross-type interaction/entropy term
future_analysis_contract_if_authorized.robustness_panel: 11 disjoint metadata-only matched pairs frozen before per-case outcomes, exact on total constraint count and metadata block, within 10 instruction words, with at least 0.35-bit type-entropy contrast
future_analysis_contract_if_authorized.direction_lock: higher cross-type entropy -> lower Partial Success Rate after controls

falsifiers: The same-information additive per-type model absorbs the cross-type entropy/interaction effect.
The pre-outcome strict matched-pair contrast is null or reverses direction without a preregistered explanation.
The apparent entropy effect disappears after frozen load/length/metadata-block controls.
The official evaluator cannot provide stable per-constraint outcomes for the qualified generator outputs without changing the scientific object.

method_intervention.candidate_only: flat instruction versus information-equivalent typed/structured constraint representation
method_intervention.forbidden_now: Do not design, tune, or run the intervention before formal Generator/ProblemGate admission.
